title: Autonomic incident choreography: handoff adaptor for trace → PD/Slack with runbook templating
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'handoff adaptor' that stitches distributed-trace signals, metric anomalies, and error logs into a compact incident payload that can be delivered to PagerDuty and Slack with an editable runbook template and one-click postmortem seed. This is intended to reduce MTTR by providing the oncall a single contextual artifact (trace snippets, latency heatmap, relevant logs, suggested remediation steps) and to enable automated postmortem creation when an incident is resolved.

Scope:
- Producer-side: tracing hook that collects prioritized span snippets and key logs (already sampled) and attaches a small context envelope.
- Orchestrator: serverless adaptor that enriches traces with metric spike evidence and chooses PD escalation level based on severity rules.
- Consumer integrations: PD webhook payloads with action buttons and Slack incident threads with a runbook template prefilled from stored procedures.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full playbook authoring UX in Console (that remains a later epic).
- Fully automated remediation; we focus on triage and handoff rather than live rollback actions in this sprint.
acceptance_criteria: PD webhook contains trace snippet (<= 3 spans) + top 3 related logs and metric delta summary
Slack incident thread message with 'Open runbook' and 'Create postmortem' buttons; clicking Create postmortem seeds a draft in Confluence/PM repo
Escalation level mapping respects account-level PD rules and per-route overrides
End-to-end latency from detection to PD/Slack delivery < 6s for P0/P1 events under normal load
Feature gated behind feature-flag and roped to audit logs for every handoff event
steps_taken: 2026-03-04: PoC tracing hook implemented in runtime: extracts top spans by error-score and attaches a 2KB context envelope (prototype branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4227)
2026-03-06: Built adaptor lambda that queries metric anomalies from telemetry service and merges into webhook payload (PR: github.com/redwood/ops-adaptors/pulls/19)
2026-03-07: Created mock Slack blocks for thread UX; experimented with button actions and ephemeral confirmations (design notes linked)
2026-03-08: Ran load test simulating 1k concurrent anomaly handoffs; average adaptor latency 120ms, 99th percentile 850ms; identified PD API rate backoff as a concern
2026-03-09: Hooked into rollout policy so Dedicated customers can opt out; added opt-in flag for Private deployments
blockers: PagerDuty API rate limits for large accounts — need token scoping or queued/batched sends; awaiting discussion with platform infra
SAML-scoped webhooks: security requires signed webhook delivery; security team requested HMAC extension on adaptor
Runbook template storage: Console schema for procedural steps needs a migration to accept structured suggestions (product validation in progress)
comments: 2026-03-05 — Marco Alvarez: Initial PoC looks good. Two asks: (1) make the trace snippet configurable by route-level policy; (2) include a short hypothesis string for the oncall to speed triage.

2026-03-07 — Priya Desai (PM): We need the slack 'Create postmortem' action to prefill the main incident fields (summary, timeline seeds, affected routes) and set visibility to the customer's default. Also flagged regulatory customers must include audit_fingerprint in payload.

2026-03-08 — Security review (Jonas Mueller): HMAC-signature on outgoing webhooks is required; adaptor needs credential rotation support. Recommend short-lived tokens for PD and signed callbacks for Slack buttons.

2026-03-09 — Design review (Sofia Li): Shared the Slack block prototype. UX feedback: move 'Create postmortem' to a confirmation modal and show 2–3 automated suggested next steps pulled from prior incidents for that route.
2026-03-10 — Marco Alvarez: Implemented HMAC header and rotation stubs; updated PR (ops-adaptors/pull/25). Next: integrate PD backoff queue and add telemetry counters for dropped handoffs.
